new.why: OpenAI published a conservative routing policy that treats replay safety as a workflow property.
new.summary: Provider-aware failover routes only repeatable AI operations to an approved secondary while preserving deadlines, controls and recovery ownership.
new.why_now: OpenAI’s October 14 guide supplies explicit eligible and blocked failure classes, retry budgets and gradual failback guidance.
new.practical_value: Test one read-only inference step across both routes and document exactly when to retry, queue, degrade or stop.

novelty.reason: The guide moves multi-provider resilience from generic routing into explicit per-operation replay and recovery decisions.

evidence.reason: OpenAI provides failure classes, implementation constraints, test cases and operational measures, though no independent outage study.

independence.reason: The guidance is authored by one model provider and lacks independent comparative validation across production gateways.

momentum.reason: This first policy observation offers no repeated comparable outcome measure for adoption, recovery time or errors.

relevance.reason: Platform and application teams can directly map retryability, deadlines, route approval and duplicate-action protection.

durability.reason: Safe retries, bounded failover and explicit recovery ownership remain necessary across providers and model generations.

momentum.reason: No two comparable dated numerical observations establish momentum for this policy.

new.why: IBM Granite combined chat, decision, guardian and speech components within one deployable checkpoint.
new.summary: Composable decision adapters activate specialized classification and safety functions beside a general chat model while reusing cached context.
new.why_now: IBM’s October 15 Granite Switch 4.1 release adds decision, guardian and speech components to 8B and 30B checkpoints.
new.practical_value: Benchmark routing, accuracy, speech quality, latency and memory on identical fixtures before replacing separate services.

novelty.reason: Combining speech, general decisions and guardian adapters in one checkpoint extends modular inference beyond chat-only composition.

evidence.reason: Model cards, code and demonstrations are available, but several performance comparisons remain publisher-reported and incomplete.

independence.reason: Open artifacts permit external testing, yet the reviewed release evidence and headline comparisons originate from IBM Granite.

momentum.reason: Release-day model cards provide no two comparable observations collected under one stable deployment or adoption metric.

relevance.reason: Teams can test whether one composed endpoint simplifies specialized decisions without sacrificing measurable workload quality.

durability.reason: Modular adapters and shared caches are durable engineering ideas even as specific checkpoints and runtimes change.

momentum.reason: No repeated comparable deployment measure supports a numeric momentum score.
